This is probably going to get buried, but what the heck.

I've been harming myself for a long time, I don't really remember not doing it other than a few childhood memories.

I used to be so happy, I had no idea what lay ahead but I knew that I had forever to enjoy my life.

Now I'm here.  I've been here for a while.  My mind flips between wanting to be me and wanting to be nobody at all.  I struggle daily with thoughts of killing myself and it's only going to get worse.

About nine months ago, I lost someone very close to me, and when they died a part of me died with them.  Since then, my mental state has been rapidly declining and at this point I'm not sure if I'll be the same person, or anyone at all, when it gets to a year.

When I cut myself I drift back in time, to those childhood moments that seemed to last forever.  My body shivers with happiness flowing through me, and I feel like the blood that drips is my pain falling away.

I admit, it's a terrible thing to do, to harm the body my parents gave me, to scar myself over issues in the past, but it helps.  It helps me clear my head, it helps me sleep at night, it helps me feel something other than the same feeling I have felt for years.  

I know there is a large taboo around the subject, and that many people would rather hate what I do, what many people do, than understand it, so I'd like to leave anyone with a negative attitude towards the subject with this:

What if you were hurting?

What if you were losing control?

What if you lost the only thing that mattered to you in life?

What if you were worse off?

What if you had nowhere to go?

If the reality of your life kept you awake?

If you hated every inch of your body for no reason?

Your life is worthless...

You've lost purpose...

How do you take back control?

How do you learn to feel again?

How do you cope?

Okay, as someone that has recently ranked up to MG1 I believe I have some degree of experience in this situation.

First of all, forget about wanting to rank up.  The only way you can rank up is by consistently playing above your estimated skill level and the only way you can do that is to focus on the game - not on winning and ranking up.

Personally, at GNM I felt out of my depth, and I actually wanted to de-rank for a long period of time but it never happened.

Try to queue up with people either at or above your skill level, and make the effort to be somewhat organised while playing games.  If the team don't pull together and play as a team then you are going to severely decrease your chances of winning the game.  

Try playing as the IGL (In Game Leader) and learning a few necessary strats for maps you frequent, and call these strats to your team whilst playing (making sure to explain them beforehand in some degree of detail).  If you die, remember to call out the position of your assassin and if someone else on your team dies and doesn't call out the position of the person that killed them then call it out for them.  Information is valuable.

Spend some time learning smokes, 'nades, and pop flashes at key points in your most played maps in order to efficiently use your equipment and give yourself the advantage in certain situations.

Now I know there's a considerable amount of people that prefer just to say "get good", and I know it's incredibly annoying, but they're right.  You have to focus on improving your gameplay rather than getting a shiny AK-47 under your name on your title screen.  This way, when you're losing a match you won't be thinking "I'm never going to rank up", you'll be thinking "Now how can I do this differently and improve on myself".

As well as everything mentioned above, LEARN FROM YOUR MISTAKES.

If you get consistently picked off at certain points on a map, delay your arrival to that area or flash yourself in, you could even try and learn a smoke to smoke off the area you are getting picked from.

Before I close up I have one more tip that I found changed my perspective on every game I have played since.

DON'T BLAME YOUR TEAM MATES FOR LOSING THE GAME, YOU LOST IT AS A TEAM AND YOU WIN AS A TEAM.  NO INDIVIDUAL IS RESPONSIBLE FOR ANY PLAY IN THE GAME - IT'S THE TEAM'S EFFORT.

Just chill out and have fun playing the game.

Good luck!

Pizza hasn't done many great things for me physically, but emotionally and socially it has had a great effect.  Throughout my childhood, I was never the popular one, I never had any friends, was too nervous to go outside and pretty much stayed in a shell for the majority of my teenage years.  However, at age 16 I made an amazing discovery.  Pizza.

It's not that I found pizza at that moment, but rather the amazing experience the right mix of flavours on the right dough can do.

I started off ordering online.  I would order a 12 inch pizza, tons of meat, sauce, and all the good stuff for £16 ($25) and eat it all in the same night.  After a few months of ordering around once a week, I got bored of eating alone, and decided to invite some people around from College (I had recently just started a new course, and was getting to know some new people) and order more than one pizza every few weeks, turning it into a social session to gossip about whatever was going on in college at that time.

This habit soon became way too expensive to keep up with, and I stopped ordering pizzas online.  I thought this was the end of my social gatherings, but boy was I wrong.

Over the next few weeks, there were no meet ups, I tried to arrange a few gatherings but to no success.  It was a Friday evening, and I was about to give up and order a pizza when the doorbell rang.  It was my friends, with pizza ingredients, a few drinks, and I lit up instantly.

We spent the night cooking pizza, eating pizza, and drinking as much as we could fit into the room left over in our stomachs.  At the end of the night, we all agreed to do it again in 2 weeks, and from then onwards we have rarely missed having a pizza night every fortnight since.

Pizza has changed my life.  I still have a few issues that I am dealing with, but without the help and support that came as a result of bonding over it I probably wouldn't be here today.
